results.summary: Let $X$ be a measurable space in which every singleton is measurable, let $\delta_{x_0}$ be the Dirac measure at a point $x_0 \in X$, and let $s \subseteq X$ be a set with $x_0 \notin s$. Then for every natural number $n \ge 1$, $\frac{1}{n} \log \delta_{x_0}(s) = -\infty$ in the extended reals, with $\log 0 = -\infty$.

results.title: Large deviation principle for a Dirac mass
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a $T_1$ topological space equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and let $x_0 \in X$. The constant sequence of measures $\mu_n = \delta_{x_0}$ satisfies the large deviation principle with the Dirac rate function of $x_0$, which is $0$ at $x_0$ and $\infty$ elsewhere.

results.title: The absolute value is a good rate function

results.title: Number of ones in a factor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an infinite binary word $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ over $\{0, 1\}$ and natural numbers $i$ and $n$, this is the number of indices $k < n$ with $x_{i+k} = 1$, that is, the number of $1$s in the factor $x_i x_{i+1} \cdots x_{i+n-1}$ of length $n$ starting at position $i$ (it is $0$ when $n = 0$).

results.title: Balanced infinite words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An infinite binary word $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ over $\{0, 1\}$ is balanced when for all natural numbers $i$, $j$ and $n$, the numbers of $1$s in the factors $x_i x_{i+1} \cdots x_{i+n-1}$ and $x_j x_{j+1} \cdots x_{j+n-1}$ of length $n$ differ by at most $1$.

results.title: Aperiodic infinite words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An infinite binary word $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ over $\{0, 1\}$ is aperiodic when it is not ultimately periodic: there are no natural numbers $p > 0$ and $N$ such that $x_{n+p} = x_n$ for all $n \ge N$.

results.title: Sturmian words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An infinite binary word $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ over $\{0, 1\}$ is Sturmian when it is both aperiodic and balanced.

results.title: RAM addressing mode
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: An addressing mode of a random-access machine specifies an operand by a natural number $n$ in one of three ways: immediate (the operand is the value $n$ itself), direct (the operand is the contents of register $n$), or indirect (the operand is the contents of the register whose index is the contents of register $n$).

results.title: RAM store destination
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A store destination of a random-access machine names, by a natural number $n$, the register into which the accumulator is stored: either register $n$ itself (direct) or the register whose index is the contents of register $n$ (indirect).

results.title: RAM instruction
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: An instruction of a random-access machine is one of the following: load an operand into the accumulator; store the accumulator into a store destination; add an operand to the accumulator; subtract an operand from the accumulator, truncating at $0$; jump to instruction $q$; jump to instruction $q$ if the accumulator is $0$; halt. Here an operand is given by a RAM addressing mode, a store destination is a RAM store…

results.title: RAM state
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A state of a random-access machine consists of a program counter in $\mathbb{N}$, an accumulator value in $\mathbb{N}$, and register contents, a function $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ giving the contents of each register.

results.title: Value of a RAM operand
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In a RAM state with register contents $r$, an operand resolves to a natural number: the immediate operand $n$ resolves to $n$ itself, the direct operand $n$ to the contents $r(n)$ of register $n$, and the indirect operand $n$ to $r(r(n))$.

results.title: Register written by a RAM store
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In a RAM state with register contents $r$, a store destination resolves to a register index: the direct destination $n$ resolves to $n$, and the indirect destination $n$ resolves to the contents $r(n)$ of register $n$.

results.title: Initial RAM state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The initial state on inputs $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ has program counter $0$ and accumulator $0$; register $i$ holds $x_i$ for $i < k$, and every other register holds $0$.

results.title: Bounded execution of a RAM machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a program $P$, a natural number $t$ and a state $s$, the state after $t$ steps of $P$ from $s$ is obtained by applying one step of $P$ to $s$ exactly $t$ times.

results.title: Output of a RAM machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be a program of length $\ell$ and $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ inputs. Run $P$ from the initial state on these inputs. If for some $t$ the program counter after $t$ steps is at least $\ell$, the output of $P$ on these inputs is the accumulator after the least such number of steps; otherwise the output is undefined.

results.title: A RAM step is sticky at halting states
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the program counter of a state $s$ is at least the length of a program $P$, then one step of $P$ leaves $s$ unchanged.

results.title: RAM execution is stable once halted
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a program of length $\ell$, $s$ a state and $t$ a natural number. If the program counter after $t$ steps of $P$ from $s$ is at least $\ell$, then the state after $t + 1$ steps of $P$ from $s$ equals the state after $t$ steps.

results.title: RAM execution stays at its halted state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a program of length $\ell$, $s$ a state and $t_1 \le t_2$ natural numbers. If the program counter after $t_1$ steps of $P$ from $s$ is at least $\ell$, then the state after $t_2$ steps of $P$ from $s$ equals the state after $t_1$ steps.

results.title: Output membership for RAM machines
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a program of length $\ell$, let $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ be inputs and let $t$ and $y$ be natural numbers. results.title: One-step unfolding functional of a while loop
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a Boolean expression $b$ (the guard) and a binary relation $B$ on states (the body relation), the functional sends a relation $R$ on states to the relation that relates $s$ to $s'$ exactly when either $b$ evaluates to false in $s$ and $s' = s$, or $b$ evaluates to true in $s$ and there is a state $m$ with $B$ relating $s$ to $m$ and $R$ relating $m$ to $s'$.

results.title: Monotonicity of the while-loop unfolding functional
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $B$ a binary relation on states, and $\Phi$ the one-step unfolding functional of a while loop with guard $b$ and body relation $B$. Then $\Phi$ is monotone for inclusion of relations: for all relations $R_1$ and $R_2$ on states with $R_1 \subseteq R_2$, we have $\Phi(R_1) \subseteq \Phi(R_2)$.

results.title: The while-loop functional as a monotone map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a boolean guard $b$ and a relation $B$ between states (the body denotation), this is the map $\Phi$ on relations between states, ordered by inclusion, where $\Phi(R)$ relates $s$ to $s'$ exactly when either $b$ is false in $s$ and $s' = s$, or $b$ is true in $s$ and there is a state $m$ with $B(s, m)$ and $R(m, s')$. The map $\Phi$ is monotone: $R_1 \subseteq R_2$ implies $\Phi(R_1) \subseteq \Phi(R_2)$.

results.title: Unfolding equation for the while denotation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Boolean expression $b$, IMP command $c$ and states $s$ and $s'$, the relational denotation of $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ relates $s$ to $s'$ if and only if either $b$ evaluates to false in $s$ and $s' = s$, or $b$ evaluates to true in $s$ and there is a state $m$ such that the denotation of $c$ relates $s$ to $m$ and the denotation of the loop relates $m$ to $s'$.

results.title: Denotational executions are big-step executions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and all states $s$ and $s'$, if the relational denotation of $c$ relates $s$ to $s'$, then executing $c$ from $s$ terminates in $s'$ according to the big-step semantics.

results.title: Big-step executions are denotational executions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and all states $s$ and $s'$, if executing $c$ from $s$ terminates in $s'$ according to the big-step semantics, then the relational denotation of $c$ relates $s$ to $s'$.

results.title: Agreement of the denotational and big-step semantics of IMP

results.title: Freivalds trial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2$, stored as arrays of rows, and a seed $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the trial computes the column vectors $Br$, $A(Br)$ and $Cr$, each by accumulating matrix products into a zero column, and returns true exactly when $A(Br) = Cr$. Its cost is the pair (number of scalar multiplications, number of scalar additions), each multiply-add step counting…

results.title: Cost of the Freivalds trial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and every seed $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the Freivalds trial performs exactly $3n^2$ scalar multiplications and exactly $3n^2$ scalar additions.

results.title: Matrix of a Freivalds input
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An $n \times n$ array $A$ of rows over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2$ determines the $n \times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$ whose $(i, j)$ entry is entry $j$ of row $i$ of $A$.

results.title: Acceptance criterion of the Freivalds trial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and every seed $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$, $r$ returns true if and only if $A(Br) = Cr$.

results.title: Acceptance via the product discrepancy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and every seed $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$, $r$ returns true if and only if $(AB - C)r = 0$.

results.title: Completeness of the Freivalds trial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with $AB = C$. Then for every seed $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$, $r$ returns true. This includes the case $n = 0$.

results.title: Freivalds trial on empty matrices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $0 \times 0$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and the empty seed $r$, the Freivalds trial returns true at zero cost: it performs no scalar multiplications and no scalar additions.

results.title: Soundness of the Freivalds trial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with $AB \ne C$. Then twice the number of seeds $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ on which the Freivalds trial returns true is at most the number of all seeds in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$; that is, at most half of the seeds accept.

results.title: Freivalds trial law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, given as arrays, the Freivalds trial law is the probability distribution on $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ of the value returned by the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ with seed $r$, where $r$ is drawn uniformly from $\mathbb{F}_2^n$.

results.title: Uniform mass of a Freivalds seed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. For every $n$ and every vector $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the uniform probability distribution on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ assigns to $r$ the probability $(2^n)^{-1}$.

results.title: Acceptance probability of the Freivalds trial as a seed count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, given as arrays. The probability that the Freivalds trial law of $A$, $B$, $C$ returns true equals the number of seeds $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ on which the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ with seed $r$ accepts, divided by the number $|\mathbb{F}_2^n|$ of all seeds.

results.title: The Freivalds trial accepts a correct product with probability one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, given as arrays. If $AB = C$, then the Freivalds trial law of $A$, $B$, $C$ returns true with probability $1$. This includes the case $n = 0$ of empty matrices.

results.title: The Freivalds trial accepts a wrong product with probability at most one half
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, given as arrays. If $AB \ne C$, then the Freivalds trial law of $A$, $B$, $C$ returns true with probability at most $1/2$.

results.title: Repeated Freivalds test on fixed seeds
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ and seeds $r_0, \dots, r_{k-1} \in (\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$, run the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ with each seed $r_0, \dots, r_{k-1}$ in order, including the trials after a rejection, and return the conjunction of their results (true when $k = 0$). The arithmetic cost of the run is the sum of the costs of the $k$ trials.

results.title: Cost of the repeated Freivalds test on fixed seeds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ and seeds $r_0, \dots, r_{k-1} \in (\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$, the repeated Freivalds test on these seeds performs exactly $3kn^2$ scalar multiplications and $3kn^2$ scalar additions.

results.title: Acceptance of the repeated Freivalds test on fixed seeds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ and seeds $r_0, \dots, r_{k-1} \in (\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$, the repeated Freivalds test on these seeds accepts if and only if, for every $i < k$, the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ with seed $r_i$ accepts.

results.title: Completeness of the repeated Freivalds test on fixed seeds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ with $AB = C$. Then for every $k$, including $k = 0$, and all seeds $r_0, \dots, r_{k-1} \in (\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$, the repeated Freivalds test on these seeds accepts.

results.title: Repeated Freivalds test with no trials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$, the repeated Freivalds test on the empty list of seeds ($k = 0$) accepts and performs no scalar multiplications or additions.

results.title: Repeated Freivalds test on empty matrices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $0 \times 0$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ and any number $k$ of seeds (each the empty vector), the repeated Freivalds test accepts and performs no scalar multiplications or additions.

results.title: Output distribution of repeated Freivalds trials
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n, k$ and $n \times n$ matrices $A, B, C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$, this is the probability distribution on $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ of the result returned by the repeated Freivalds executor on $A, B, C$ when its history of $k$ seeds is drawn uniformly from $(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^k$.

results.title: Uniform mass of a Freivalds seed history
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, under the uniform distribution on histories of $k$ seeds, that is, on $(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^k$, every history has probability exactly $(2^{nk})^{-1}$. This includes the cases $k = 0$ and $n = 0$.

results.title: Counting accepted histories of repeated Freivalds trials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n, k$ be natural numbers and let $A, B, C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$. The number of histories $(r_1, \dots, r_k)$ of seeds $r_i \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ on which the repeated Freivalds executor accepts equals $a^k$, where $a$ is the number of seeds $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ on which a single Freivalds trial accepts.

results.title: Acceptance probability of repeated Freivalds trials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n, k$ be natural numbers and let $A, B, C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$. If the history of $k$ seeds is drawn uniformly from $(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^k$, the probability that the repeated Freivalds executor accepts is $p^k$, where $p$ is the probability that a single Freivalds trial accepts on a seed drawn uniformly from $\mathbb{F}_2^n$.

results.title: Completeness of repeated Freivalds trials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n, k$ be natural numbers and let $A, B, C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with $AB = C$. If the history of $k$ seeds is drawn uniformly from $(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^k$, then the repeated Freivalds executor accepts with probability $1$.

results.title: Soundness of repeated Freivalds trials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n, k$ be natural numbers and let $A, B, C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with $AB \ne C$. If the history of $k$ seeds is drawn uniformly from $(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^k$, then the repeated Freivalds executor accepts with probability at most $(2^k)^{-1}$.

results.title: The sharp Freivalds example has a wrong product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A = B = (1)$ and $C = (0)$ be $1 \times 1$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. Then $AB \neq C$.

results.title: The sharp Freivalds example accepts exactly the zero seed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A = B = (1)$ and $C = (0)$ be $1 \times 1$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. For every seed $r \in (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^1$, the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ with seed $r$, which compares $A(Br)$ with $Cr$, accepts if and only if the single entry $r_0$ of $r$ is $0$.

results.title: The sharp Freivalds example has exactly one accepted seed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A = B = (1)$ and $C = (0)$ be $1 \times 1$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. Exactly one seed $r \in (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^1$ is accepted by the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$.

results.title: The sharp Freivalds example is accepted with probability one half
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A = B = (1)$ and $C = (0)$ be $1 \times 1$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. When the seed is drawn uniformly from $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^1$, the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ accepts with probability exactly $1/2$.

results.title: Exact acceptance probability of repeated trials on the sharp Freivalds example
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A = B = (1)$ and $C = (0)$ be $1 \times 1$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, and let $k$ be a natural number. Run $k$ Freivalds trials on $A$, $B$, $C$ with seeds drawn independently and uniformly from $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^1$, accepting exactly when every trial accepts. Then the run accepts with probability exactly $2^{-k}$.
